Rashi on Nedarim 15a:10:1.hebrew: אם הלכה - לבית אביה קודם הפסח, אסורה להנות ממנו קודם הפסח כמו שנדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:10:1.english: If she went - to her father's house before Passover, she is prohibited from deriving benefit from him before Passover, just as he vowed.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:10:2.hebrew: הא אם לא הלכה - לפני הפסח, אינה אסורה עד הפסח, ולא חיישינן שמא תלך לאחר הפסח ונמצאת למפרע נהנית באיסור. וקשה לרב יהודה דאמר "אל יישן היום שמא יישן למחר", דאם איתא לדרב יהודה, הוה אסר לה מתני' עד הפסח אפי' אם לא הלכה עד הפסח, דחיישינן שמא תלך לאחר הפסח ונמצאת נהנית ממנו באיסורא:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:10:2.english: But if she did not go - before Passover, she is not prohibited [from benefiting from him] until Passover, and we are not concerned lest she go after Passover and be found retroactively to have derived benefit in [a state of] prohibition. And [this] is difficult according to Rav Yehuda, who said, "He should not sleep today lest he sleep tomorrow," for if it were as Rav Yehuda [maintains], the Mishnah would have prohibited her [from benefiting] until Passover even if she had not gone until Passover, since we would be concerned lest she go after Passover and be found to have derived benefit from him in [a state of] prohibition.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:11:2.hebrew: אמר ר' אבא - תריץ הכי למתניתין: הלכה לפני הפסח, אסורה בהנאתו ולוקה, דעוברת על בל יחל. ואם לא הלכה לפני הפסח, ואפילו הכי אסורה בהנאתו עד הפסח איסורא בעלמא, דחיישינן שמא תלך לאחר הפסח ונמצאת נהנית למפרע באיסורא:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:11:2.english: Rabbi Abba said - [He] explains our Mishnah thus: [If] she went before Passover, she is prohibited from deriving benefit from him and is flogged, for she transgresses [the prohibition of] "he shall not profane [his word]." And if she did not go before Passover, even so she is prohibited from deriving benefit from him until Passover [as] a mere prohibition, for we are concerned lest she go after Passover, and it will turn out [that] she was deriving benefit retroactively in [a state of] prohibition.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:11:3.hebrew: הלכה - חייבת מלקות, דהא עברה. הכי מסקנא דמתני': הלכה לאחר הפסח, עוברת משום בל יחל:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:11:3.english: She went - [She is] liable for lashes, for she has transgressed [her vow]. Thus [is] the conclusion of the Mishnah: [If] she went after Passover, she transgresses [the prohibition of] "he shall not profane [his word]."

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:12:1.hebrew: ומקשינן מינה: ואי דלא איתהני לפני הפסח, מי איכא "בל יחל":
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:12:1.english: And we raise an objection from it [the latter clause]: And if she did not derive benefit before Passover, is there [a transgression of] "He shall not profane"?

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:12:2.hebrew: אלא לאו פשיטא דאיתהני - לפני הפסח, וסברה לא אלך אחר הפסח, והלכה לאחר הפסח:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:12:2.english: Rather, is it not obvious that she derived benefit - before Passover, and she thought, "I will not go after Passover," and she went after Passover.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:1:1.hebrew: כי לא מיזדהר בתנאיה - דכיון דיום של מחר הוי תנאיה ליום אתמול — כגון דאמר קונם עיני בשינה היום אם אישן למחר — הוי אותו היום דלמחר תנאי לאותו היום דאתמול, דאם יישן למחר הוי לקי מאותו שינה דאתמול, ואם לא יישן לא לקי. משום הכי אמרינן דלא יישן היום, דשמא כי אתי למחר לא מיזדהר בתנאי ונמצא עובר בבל יחל:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:1:1.english: When one is not careful, [it is] with regard to his condition - Since tomorrow is the condition for yesterday — for example, where he said, "Konam [be] my eyes with respect to sleep today if I sleep tomorrow" — that tomorrow is a condition for that yesterday, for if he sleeps tomorrow he incurs lashes for that sleep of yesterday, and if he does not sleep he does not incur lashes. Therefore, we say that he may not sleep today, lest when tomorrow arrives he will not be careful about the condition and will end up transgressing [the prohibition of] "he shall not profane [his word]."

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:1:2.hebrew: אבל באיסורא - דאמר קונם עיני בשינה מחר אם אישן היום, דאותו יום של מחר נטוי לאיסורא, ודאי מיזהר זהיר ביה. דאי לא מיזהר, מקיים תנאי שישן באותו היום, ודאי כי אתי למחר לא הוי ישן, דהא איתסר בנדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:1:2.english: However, with regard to a prohibition - Where he said, "Konam [be] my eyes in sleep tomorrow if I sleep today," since that day of tomorrow is poised for prohibition, he will certainly be careful with it. For if [he is] not [careful, and] fulfills the condition that he sleeps on that day, certainly when tomorrow comes he will not sleep, since he is prohibited by the vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:2:1.english: If we say [it is] as it teaches, "[Konam] that I sleep," is it a vow - Behold, sleep is something that has no substance.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:2:2.english: Rather, where he says, "Sleeping is konam for my eyes" - And the eye regarding which he vowed has actual substance.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:3:1.english: And if he did not give a measurement - [Specifying] for how long a time he will not sleep.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:3:2.hebrew: מי שבקינן ליה - הא עבר ודאי באיסור לא יחל, דלא מצי למיקם בנפשיה דלא יישן:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:3:2.english: Do we leave him [be] - Surely he will certainly transgress the prohibition of "he shall not profane," for he cannot restrain himself from sleeping.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:3:3.hebrew: והאמר ר' יוחנן וכו' - לאלתר מלקין אותו שיישן, הואיל דנדר בדבר שאין יכול לעמוד בו:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:3:3.english: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say, etc. - Immediately they flog him so that he may sleep, since he vowed regarding something that he cannot uphold.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:5:1.hebrew: ואי לא ניים היום כי ניים למחר מאי איסור בל יחל איכא - דקתני אסור, והרי לא ישן אתמול כלום:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:5:1.english: And if he does not sleep today, when he sleeps tomorrow, what prohibition of "he shall not profane" is there - For [the Mishnah] teaches [that it is] forbidden, yet he did not sleep at all yesterday.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:5:2.hebrew: אלא בדניים - אתמול, דהכי מיירי מתניתין: אם יישן היום ויישן למחר, אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:5:2.english: Rather, [is it not] where he slept - Yesterday, for this is what the Mishnah is discussing: if he sleeps today and sleeps tomorrow, it is forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:5:3.hebrew: אלמא אית ליה דניים - אלמא דשבקינן ליה לישן היום, ולא חיישינן שמא יישן למחר, ותיובתא דרב יהודה:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:5:3.english: Apparently, he has [a case] where he sleeps - Apparently, we allow him to sleep today, and we are not concerned lest he sleep tomorrow; and [this is] a refutation of Rav Yehuda.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:6:1.hebrew: אמר לך רב יהודה: הכי קתני <abbr title="מתניתין">מתני'</abbr>, "קונם שאני בשינה היום אם אישן למחר" — דאסור כי ניים למחר, דאי ניים מאתמול, דיעבד; אבל לכתחילה אין מניחין אותו לישן היום, דחיישינן שמא יישן למחר:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:6:1.english: Rav Yehudah would say to you: This is what the Mishnah teaches — [regarding] "Konam that I [benefit] from sleep today if I sleep tomorrow" — that he is forbidden when he sleeps tomorrow, [meaning] that if he slept yesterday [it is] after the fact; but ab initio we do not allow him to sleep today, because we are concerned lest he sleep tomorrow.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:7:1.hebrew: לעולם כדקתני - שאיני ישן. והאי דקאמר "והא שינה דבר שאין בו ממש וליכא בל יחל" — ודאי מדאורייתא ליכא בל יחל, ומאי "בל יחל" איכא דקתני מתניתין? דאסור מדרבנן:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:7:1.english: Actually, as it teaches - [That is,] "that I will not sleep." And [as for] that which [the Gemara] asks, "But sleep is something that has no substance, and there is no [prohibition of] 'he shall not profane'" — certainly, by Torah law there is no [prohibition of] "he shall not profane." And what [prohibition of] "he shall not profane" is there that the Mishnah teaches? That it is forbidden by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:8:1.english: But is there [a prohibition of] “he shall not profane” by rabbinic law - That we flog him by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:8:2.hebrew: אי אתה רשאי לנהוג בהן היתר לפניהם - לבטל מנהגם, דעובר משום בל יחל. ומן התורה אינו בבל יחל, אלא מדרבנן:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:8:2.english: You are not permitted to treat them as permitted in their presence - To nullify their custom, as he transgresses [the prohibition of] "he shall not profane." And by Torah law it is not [subject to] "he shall not profane," but rather [only] by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Nedarim 15a:9:1.hebrew: קונם שאת נהנית לי עד הפסח אם תלכי לבית אביך מכאן עדי החג - בפ' הנודר מן הירק. כגון דקאי באדר ואמר: קונם תהא הנאתי עליך — מאכל ומשקה — עד הפסח, אם תלכי לבית אביך מכאן עד החג — עד סוכות:
Rashi on Nedarim 15a:9:1.english: Konam [that] you derive benefit from me until Passover if you go to your father's house from now until the Festival - [This Mishnah is] in the chapter [entitled] HaNoder Min HaYerek. For example, [a case] where he is in Adar and said: "Konam shall my benefit be upon you — [namely,] food and drink — until Passover, if you go to your father's house from now until the Festival" — [meaning] until Sukkot.

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:2:1.hebrew: תנן שאת נהנית לי עד הפסח וכו' - תימה: הא משעבד לה, והיכי מצי מדיר לה? וי"ל: באומר "קונם תשמישך עלי", ו"שאת נהנית לי" לאו דוקא. אי נמי: שאני הכא, כיון שתולה הנדר בדבר שיכולה לקיים, שפיר חייל הנדר אף כי מדירה כשאמר "קונם תשמישי עליך", שהרי לא תלך לבית אביה ולא תיאסר. הלכה — אין, לא הלכה — לא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:2:1.english: We learned [in the Mishnah]: "That you derive benefit from me until Pesach, etc." - This is astonishing: he is obligated to her [for marital relations], so how can he impose a vow upon her? And one can say: [The Mishnah is speaking] of one who says, "Your marital intimacy is konam upon me," and [the wording] "that you derive benefit from me" is imprecise. Alternatively: Here it is different; since he makes the vow contingent on something that she can fulfill, the vow validly takes effect even though he imposes the vow upon her when he says, "My marital intimacy is konam upon you," for she will not go to her father's house and [thus] will not become forbidden. [That is, if] she went — yes [she is forbidden]; [if] she did not go — no [she is not forbidden].

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:2:2.hebrew: אלא דאמר קונם עיני היום וכו', אלמא איתא דניים - והיא גופ' אשמעי', דאתיא לידי אסור בל יחל מתוך שמותר לישן היום. וא"ת: ולוקמיה כגון דאמר "קונם עיני בשינה למחר אם אישן היום", דבההיא מודה רב יהודה? וי"ל: דהא נמי מילתא דפשיטא היא, ולא איצטריך לאשמוע':
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:2:2.english: Rather, where he said: "My eyes are konam [in sleep] today, etc." — evidently he may sleep [today] - And that very point teaches us that he comes to the prohibition of "he shall not profane" [his word] as a result of being permitted to sleep today. And if you will ask: Let us establish [the Mishnah] as referring to a case where he said, "My eyes are konam in sleep tomorrow if I sleep today," for in that [case] Rav Yehuda agrees [that he may sleep today]? And one can answer: That too is an obvious matter, and it was not necessary to teach [it to] us.

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:3:1.hebrew: ואי דלא יהיב שיעורא מי שבקיניה עד דעבר איסורא בל יחל והא א"ר יוחנן שבועה שלא אישן שלשה ימים וכו' - מכאן פר"י דנדר שאי אפשר לקיים אינו חל, דהכא מדמי נדר שא"א לקיימו לשבועת שוא. וההוא דנדר מכל פרי דעלמא (דף עט:) — לאו דוקא כל פרי, דא"כ לא הוה חייל, כיון דאי אפשר לקיים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:3:1.english: "And if he did not give a measurement, do we let him be until he transgresses the prohibition of 'he shall not profane'? But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say: 'An oath that I will not sleep for three days,' etc." - From here, Ri explained that a vow that is impossible to fulfill does not take effect, for here [the Gemara] compares a vow that is impossible to fulfill to a vain oath. And that [case] where one vowed [to abstain] from every fruit in the world (79b) — [it means] not literally every fruit, for if so, it would not have taken effect, since it is impossible to fulfill.

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:5:1.hebrew: אלא דאמר קונם עיני היום וכו' אלמא איתא דניים - והיא גופ' אשמעי', דאתיא לידי אסור בל יחל מתוך שמותר לישן היום. וא"ת: ולוקמיה כגון דאמר "קונם עיני בשינה למחר אם אישן היום", דבההיא מודה רב יהודה? וי"ל: דהא נמי מילתא דפשיטא היא, ולא איצטריך לאשמועי':
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:5:1.english: "Rather, [it is obvious] that he said: '[Sleeping is] konam to my eyes today, etc.' Apparently, there is [a situation] in which he sleeps" - And this itself teaches us that one comes to the prohibition of "he shall not profane [his word]" because he is permitted to sleep today. And if you ask: Let us establish [the mishna] as referring to a case where he said, "Sleeping is konam to my eyes tomorrow if I sleep today," for in that [case] Rav Yehuda agrees [that he may sleep today]? One can say: That too is an obvious matter, and it was not necessary to teach it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:6:1.hebrew: כי קתני דאי ניים - וא"ת: פשיטא דאם ניים דהוה בבל יחל! ויש לומר: דההיא גופא אתא לאשמועינן, דאסור לישן היום כדרב יהודה. וה"ק: הרי זה בלא יחל דברו — כלומר, יש לו ליזהר שלא ישן, שאם ישן יבא לידי בל יחל דברו, דשמא ישן למחר, דמתנאי לא מזדהר, כדר' יהודה; לכך אם ישן היום, קרוב לודאי הוא שיבא לידי בל יחל דברו, לפי שרגילות הוא שישן למחר, כדפרישי' דבתנאי לא מזדהר. וא"ת: ולוקמא כגון דיהיב שיעורא לשינתו, ועכשיו לא קשיא ההיא דרבי יוחנן? וי"ל: דהאי נמי פשיטא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:6:1.english: When [the Mishnah] teaches [this, it means] that if he slept - And if you ask: It is obvious that if he slept [today and also sleeps tomorrow], he is in [violation of] "he shall not profane [his word]"! One can say: It comes to teach us that very point—that it is forbidden to sleep today, in accordance with Rav Yehudah. And this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: "Behold, this person is [in violation of] 'he shall not profane his word'" — meaning, he must be careful not to sleep [today], for if he sleeps [today], he will come to [violate] "he shall not profane his word," since perhaps he will sleep tomorrow, as [a person] is not careful regarding a condition, in accordance with Rav Yehudah; therefore, if he sleeps today, it is nearly certain that he will come to [violate] "he shall not profane his word," because it is usual for him to sleep tomorrow, as we explained that one is not careful regarding a condition. And if you ask: Let us establish [the Mishnah] in a case where he gave a limit to his sleep, and now that [statement] of Rabbi Yochanan would not be difficult? One can say: That too is obvious.

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:7:1.hebrew: רבינא אמר לעולם כדקתני - שאני ישן. ואע"ג דהוי דבר שאין בו ממש, מ"מ אסור מדרבנן, ו"בל יחל" דקתני — אסמכתא בעלמא. ומיהו גבי "קונם שאני משמשך" מודה רבינא דאיכא "בל יחל" מדאורייתא, והוי מתני' לצדדין: גבי "שאני ישן" הוי "בל יחל" מדרבנן, וגבי "קונם שאני משמשך" הוי "בל יחל" מדאורייתא. ונראה דהלכה כרבינא, דאמר דאפילו דבר שאין בו ממש איכא "בל יחל" מדרבנן: חדא, דרבינא בתראה; ועוד, כ"ע סבירא להו כרבינא. והא דדחיק הש"ס לשנויי "דאי ניים" ולא מתרץ כרבינא — לא משום דלית ליה דרבינא, אלא משום דמשמע ליה מתניתין דקתני "בל יחל" גבי "שאני ישן" דוקא קאמר מדאורייתא, דומיא דגבי "שאני משמשך" דתני בהדייהו; ורבינא לא חייש להכי. הלכך, הנודר "שאני ישן", "שאני מדבר", וכן כל דבר שאין בו ממש — צריך התרת חכם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:7:1.english: Ravina said: Actually, [it is] as it teaches - [i.e.,] "that I sleep." Even though it is an intangible matter [lit., something that has no substance], nevertheless it is prohibited by rabbinic law, and [the prohibition of] "he shall not profane" that [the Mishnah] teaches is a mere asmakhta [textual support]. However, with regard to "konam that I have marital relations with you," Ravina concedes that there is [a prohibition of] "he shall not profane" by Torah law, and the Mishnah is [taught] in two distinct parts: with regard to "that I sleep," it is [a prohibition of] "he shall not profane" by rabbinic law, whereas with regard to "konam that I have marital relations with you," it is [a prohibition of] "he shall not profane" by Torah law. And it appears [to us] that the halakhah follows Ravina, who said that even [with] an intangible matter there is [a prohibition of] "he shall not profane" by rabbinic law: first, because Ravina is the later [authority]; and furthermore, everyone agrees with Ravina. And [as for] that which the Gemara strains to answer "that if he sleeps," and does not explain [the Mishnah] like Ravina — [it is] not because it disagrees with Ravina, rather because it seemed to [the Gemara] that the Mishnah, which teaches "he shall not profane" regarding "that I sleep," means it literally by Torah law, similar to "that I have marital relations with you," which is taught alongside it; whereas Ravina is not concerned about this. Therefore, one who vows "that I sleep," [or] "that I speak," and similarly [regarding] any intangible matter — requires absolution by a sage.

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:8:1.hebrew: ואחרים נהגו בו איסור - תימה: מה ענין זה לנהגו בו איסור? וי"ל, דהאי נמי שנדר ונתכוון לאסור עצמו גם בדבר שאין בו ממש — אין לך נהגו גדול מזה. כ"נ למשי"ח:
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:8:1.english: "But others are accustomed to observe a prohibition with regard to it" - This is surprising: what connection does this [case] have to ["they] are accustomed to observe a prohibition with regard to it"? And one can answer that [in] this [case] as well, where one vowed and intended to forbid himself even in something that has no substance — there is no greater [instance of] "they are accustomed" than this. So it appears to Mashiach.

Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:9:1.hebrew: תנן שאת נהנית לי עד הפסח וכו' - תימה: הא משעבד לה, והיכי מצי מדיר לה? וי"ל: באומר "קונם תשמישך עלי", ושאת נהנית לי לאו דוקא. אי נמי: שאני הכא, כיון שתולה הנדר בדבר שיכולה לקיים, שפיר חייל הנדר אף כי מדירה כשאמר "קונם תשמישי עליך", שהרי לא תלך לבית אביה ולא תיאסר. הלכה — אין, לא הלכה — לא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 15a:9:1.english: We learned [in a Mishnah]: "That you derive benefit from me until Passover, etc." - [This is] astonishing: behold, he is obligated to her, so how can he prohibit her by a vow? And one can say: [This refers to a case] where he says, "Your marital relations are konam to me," and [the phrasing] "that you derive benefit from me" is imprecise. Alternatively: Here it is different, [for] since he makes the vow dependent on something that she is able to fulfill, the vow takes effect validly even though he is prohibiting her when he said, "My marital relations are konam to you" — for she will simply not go to her father's house and will not become prohibited. [If] she went — yes [she is prohibited]; [if] she did not go — no [she is not prohibited].
